title: Worked example — Continuity Plan Helper
lede: A generic GOV Assured-style community web app, with no personal names. This is an illustrative walk-through, not a complete threat model.
setup: People complete a form about continuity needs and can optionally save a draft.
A cloud model API generates a draft plan.
Drafts are stored in a database.
The home page also shows a public threat dashboard whose items link out to their sources.
The service is built and deployed through CI/CD to a cloud platform, with a service identity for the model API.

steps.title: Scope
steps.text: This service, including the model API, the database, the public feed, identities and the pipeline; not the rest of the GOV Assured estate.

steps.title: Landscape
steps.text: Opportunistic web attackers, abuse of the model API, supply-chain compromise of a dependency or the pipeline; catalogues: ATT&CK v20.1, ATLAS 2026.10, OWASP LLM Top 10 2026 (prompt injection, sensitive disclosure, excessive agency, supply chain).

steps.title: Model
steps.text: Browser → app → database; app → model API; app → external feeds; CI/CD → production; identity and service credentials.

steps.title: Assets and boundaries
steps.text: Draft plan content, prompts and outputs, model API credentials, feed integrity, community reputation; trust boundaries at each of those hops.

steps.title: Threats
steps.text: Examples: spoofed or tampered feed items; another organisation’s draft being disclosed; prompt injection into the model; the service identity for the model being stolen from the pipeline; a poisoned dependency.

steps.title: Prioritise
steps.text: Information disclosure of drafts, abuse of the model API, and pipeline compromise typically outrank cosmetic defacement; include untrue or over-confident plan text as an AI-specific harm.

steps.title: Mitigations
steps.text: Least-privilege service identity, no secrets in prompts or logs, signed builds / provenance, output handling, rate limits, owner-accepted residual risk for a public feed that only links to sources.

steps.title: Validate
steps.text: Tests for access control on drafts; a GenAI red-team pass for prompt injection; a check that detection would notice credential misuse.

steps.title: Record
steps.text: A version-controlled model file plus a short pack, dated and owned.

steps.title: Continuous
steps.text: Re-open when the model provider, the feed, or a major dependency changes; pipeline warns if the model file is stale.
